name: local-moe-fugu-7940hs
purpose: Sequential MoE-of-MoEs conductor for Windows 11 + Ryzen 9 7940HS + 64GB RAM using llama.cpp router mode.
warnings: Do not run three 30B-class MoE GGUF models resident/parallel on a 64GB RAM mini PC.
Use llama.cpp router mode with --models-max 2 for the current Gemma/Qwen/GLM worker mix.
Verify actual model IDs via llama.cpp /v1/models before using local filename mode.
Streaming returns the final answer only (internal draft/critique/verify are not streamed).
Run uvicorn with --workers 1; the anti-fanout lock is per-process.
For SSH-launched persistent runtime on Windows, use restart_fugu_stack_user.ps1 so Scheduled Tasks own the long-running processes.
The frontdoor now honors client max_tokens / max_completion_tokens and shrinks internal deep/ultra stage budgets for short requests.
The mini PC router profile enables cache_prompt, cache-idle-slots, reasoning off, q8 KV cache, --models-max 2, and draft-free ngram-cache speculative decoding.
The default scheduler uses fast_bias and does not run verifier calls for ordinary code tasks unless verification is explicitly requested.
The fast primary is biased to Qwen on this hardware; Gemma is preserved mainly for planner/synthesis and heavier workflows.
Japanese non-code prompts are biased back to Gemma because Qwen3-Coder is unreliable for Japanese general responses on this setup.
Non-stream responses include system_fingerprint.performance with actual TPS, theoretical TPS, backend prefill/decode TPS, overhead, and model call timings.
The theoretical TPS is computed from llama.cpp timings for the exact routed request, not from isolated worker microbenchmarks.
Japanese fast prompts use compact local context hints and deterministic visible Latin a-count correction where applicable.

A narrow Japanese compound prompt path handles weekday/date, integral basics, ice-cream moderation, 50m travel choice, and visible vowel/character counts deterministically without a worker model call.
Japanese quoted-a counts are reported as visible-text counts: hiragana only, hiragana/katakana variants, and visible kana a-row; Kanji-derived phonetic readings are not guessed.
Standalone count prompts now use deterministic_count for Latin vowel-a, Japanese quoted-a vowel, and generic quoted-string counting before worker routing.
Count prompts with lead-ins such as next text / following text count only the target text after the first newline or colon when detected.
scripts/bench_fugu_japanese.py checks the FUGU bundle, not individual workers, for Japanese deterministic compound and count behavior.
Simple exact-answer arithmetic and weekday multiple-choice prompts may be answered by deterministic front paths without a worker model call.
Long prompts are clipped with head+tail middle omission in both conductor and 0.6B router so leading instructions are preserved.
Long lookup-like prompts use FUGU retrieval context packing: head, tail, and query-relevant middle excerpts are retained before worker routing.
Short explicit code/command/function requests use a compact fast prompt to avoid tutorial-length completions.
Short follow-up prompts can keep the previous conversation's primary worker via followup affinity; Japanese general followups are still protected from being dragged back to Qwen.

Explicit output-shape requests such as return exactly ANSWER, return exactly `literal`, or return only the expression are enforced after model generation; exact-answer fast routes also get a smaller generation cap.
Safe exact literal prompts are answered deterministically before worker routing; marker-visibility exact prompts require the literal tokens to be visible outside the quoted target.
Forced deep/ultra aliases use compact Qwen paths for short max_tokens requests, while uncapped requests keep the heavier multi-stage workflows.
Output cleanup removes dangling empty section headings such as a trailing Explanation: label.
Tool execution metadata is returned in system_fingerprint.performance as tool_call_count, tool_fail_count, tool_call_wall_ms, and tool_calls.

The /fugu/capabilities endpoint reports the active MAX-mode feature matrix: workers, mode aliases, 0.6B control tower state, deterministic paths, retrieval context policy, tool policy, runtime fanout constraints, and telemetry.
scripts/audit_fugu_runtime.py --include-heavy verifies the real non-compact deep and ultra quality workflows, not only the fast compact aliases.
scripts/audit_fugu_runtime.py --only-heavy can retest the non-compact deep/ultra quality workflows without rerunning the full normal audit set.
scripts/run_clean_speed_gate.ps1 restarts/warmups the mini PC stack, benchmarks the whole FUGU frontdoor, and fails if correctness or clean-speed TPS regress.
fugu_tools now runs even when a deterministic route answered first, because explicit tool requests should not be silently ignored.
The local tool whitelist includes standard-library python -m unittest in addition to pytest/ruff/npm/tsc checks.
A narrow visible-artifact cleanup fixes the Cyrillic connector that Qwen occasionally emits in short workflow lists.
ANSWER-only and other explicit exact fast routes pass stop sequences to the backend to end generation before same-line explanations.
Long exact retrieval prompts under 20000 characters can stay on the fast path instead of paying for verifier workflows.

scripts/audit_fugu_runtime.py checks health, router_06b loaded state, model listing, deterministic paths, worker routing, output artifacts, performance metadata, optional mode aliases, optional API streaming/tool checks, and short-followup primary affinity against the whole FUGU endpoint.
router_06b uses Qwen3-0.6B hidden states for routing when its dependencies/model are installed, and falls back to the rules router otherwise.
Qwen3-0.6B-Q8_0.gguf can be used for Qwen-only draft experiments via configs/llama_models_minipc_preset.ini, but it benchmarked slower than ngram-cache only and is not enabled by default.
restart_fugu_stack_user.ps1 performs Gemma-Japanese/Qwen-code warmup by default after health checks; pass -SkipWarmup for launcher experiments.
scripts/run_vulkan_trial.ps1 benchmarks the AMD Radeon 780M iGPU/Vulkan backend against the whole FUGU endpoint; it is not the production persistent launcher.
The production stack now uses a hybrid CPU/iGPU split: Qwen primary calls use the AMD Radeon 780M Vulkan backend on port 8081, while Gemma/GLM and fallback use CPU b9784 on port 8080.
Version 0.7.8 tunes both backend profiles: CPU uses threads=8, threads-batch=16, q8 KV, flash-attn on; Vulkan uses threads=16, batch=512, ubatch=512, f16 KV, flash-attn on, -ngl 99.

Version 0.7.9 keeps the production Vulkan backend on b8992, runs llama.cpp/frontdoor processes at High priority, and leaves --poll unset by default because end-to-end FUGU tests beat explicit Poll50/Poll100 for average latency/TPS.
